newsitem.title: USA: Rain seen in most of the U.S. Midwest this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Rain seen in most of the U.S. Midwest this weekend.

text.p: Most of the U.S. Midwest is expected to receive rains ranging from 0.25 to 1.50 inches this weekend, U.S. meteorologists said.

"We're looking at a wet weather pattern for the next week to 10 days," said Jim Roemer, with Roemer Weather in Raleigh, N.C. "I'm looking for 0.50 inch to an inch with 70 percent (rainfall) coverage."
The rain is considered critical for soybeans as much of the crop enters the pod-filling stage. Good moisture during pod-fill typcially bolsters yields, meteorologists and crop observers said.'
Fred Gesser, with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb. expects 0.25 to 1.50 inch of rain to fall in southern South Dakota, northeastern Nebraska and Iowa Saturday night through Sunday morning.
"This is going to be a very important rain for Iowa soybeans," Gesser said.
There are parts of Iowa, including Mason City and Des Moines that have had August rainfall totals that are 30 to 40 percent of normal levels, Gesser said.
In the eastern Corn Belt, most of the dry areas in central Illinois and Indiana received rain over the past 24 hours.

Thunderstorms broke out in virually all of Illinois after midnight on Thursday and "basically all sections of the Midwest have now received significant rains during the past six days," a report from Jon Davis with Smith Barney said.
Gesser said that midday weather models on Friday indicated there is a chance that Saturday and early Sunday in the western Corn Belt could be drier than expected.
"I'm countering the models, but the midday models are definitely the driest for Iowa and eastern Nebraska, he said."
Temperatures across the Corn Belt this weekend should be warmer, with highs in the low 80s to 90s degrees Fahrenheit, according to Davis.
Monday through Wednesday, cooler air will move into the Midwest and highs will be in the mid-70s to mid-80s before warm weather moves in again late week, he said.
